_comment: Daedalus's policy for its OWN repository. Authorised by Kaya on 2026-07-29. See docs/PROPOSED_SELF_POLICY.md for the reasoning and docs/adrs/ for the write-confinement finding. To revoke: delete this file. There is no other state.
name: agent_env
_comment_team: The windowed documentation writer is pinned to the measured 14B bench model. qwen3.6 spent bounded generations in hidden reasoning or preserved the obsolete identifier; qwen2.5-coder:14b used the supplied current-code context and produced the exact resolving replacement in a one-line splice.
_comment_gardener_queue: Candidate-base freeze for the 2026-09-29 gardener campaign. The narrow write policy and disabled inferred picker sources are present in this revision, but the repo-local queue is deliberately disabled so a candidate worktree cannot recursively pick campaign tasks. A later control commit activates the queue and binds its repo_state.head to this exact revision.

policy._comment_write_allow: THIS is the write permission. `allow` below is the EGRESS axis and does NOT gate writes. Owner direction 2026-08-29 adds only the Masterplan destinations needed by the bounded Fourfold/Tensor gardener: daedalus/twin/ and daedalus/evolution/. The broader kernel, runtime, orchestration, spine, policy, budget and promotion surfaces remain outside this campaign. write_allow is prefix-anchored at the repo root: an entry ending in / names a subtree, anything else names one file.
policy._comment_egress: Which paths' BYTES may reach an untrusted external API. Separate question from writing, deliberately kept separate. | 2026-07-30, owner decision: 'daedalus/' added so external review lanes (DeepSeek) can READ the package source. This is an EGRESS widening and nothing else -- default_deny stays true, the deny list is checked BEFORE this allow list so secrets/.env/credentials/keys remain blocked, write_allow is independent, and external_write_lanes stays [] so an external lane still cannot APPLY anything. runs/ and .agentenv/ are deliberately NOT added: the ledger, receipts and room transcripts are operational history, not source.
policy._comment_high_risk: Belt to write_allow's braces, and it does real work even though write_allow already denies these: it forces change_risk -> 'high', which routes the task AWAY from the free local lane before any write is attempted. If somebody widens write_allow later -- and somebody will -- these must still be refused, so that widening has to delete a line that names what it is protecting.
policy._comment_external_write_lanes: Which UNTRUSTED external provider lanes may APPLY a change instead of only advising. Empty (the default, and today's behaviour) = every external lane is advisory-only. This campaign does not change that: external review may advise, but only an already admitted local writer can produce a candidate, and every candidate remains held for owner review.

_comment_write_wave_policy: Iron Plan revision 1 (owner adoption 2026-07-30) separates candidate nomination from sealed owner-controlled promotion. Concurrent write waves therefore remain held for a human even when the discrimination receipt is fresh. Changing this value requires an Iron Plan amendment; an integration worktree is still a promotion surface, not a semantic exception.
_comment_test: The verify gate after a live write. Deliberately the WHOLE suite, not a scoped subset: write_allow permits tests/, so a candidate can write a test, and a scoped command would not necessarily run the file the candidate just added. -x stops at the first failure, which is the only outcome that matters to a gate. RE-EXAMINED 2026-07-29 against the argument that docs/ writes cannot break Python tests and so deserve a cheaper gate: that argument is FALSE here, measured. tests/test_comms.py:27 reads the real docs/COMMS_PROTOCOL.md, tests/test_generated_inventory.py reads the real docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.json and docs/architecture-state.json, and tests/test_markdown_nodes.py:350 reads the real docs/HANDOFF.md. write_allow permits docs/, so a docs-only candidate can genuinely turn this suite red. The whole-suite command stays.
_comment_test_timeout: MEASURED 2026-07-29: this file declared the whole suite while verifier.verify() hard-coded timeout_s=120 and offload passed nothing else, so the committed configuration was STRUCTURALLY unable to pass -- every live write died with 'could not run tests: ... timed out after 120 seconds' and rolled back before the gate was ever reached. This budget is a RUNAWAY guard, not a performance target: it exists to stop a wedged pytest from pinning the harness, so it is sized well ABOVE the observed runtime rather than tightly around it. A false timeout is expensive in both directions -- good work is rolled back AND the task escalates to a paid lane -- and this box runs several agents at once, so a suite that takes ~20 min idle can take considerably longer under load. Hence roughly 2x headroom. Consequence to accept knowingly: every live write to an admitted path pays the full suite. The real fix for that is evidence-backed path-aware test selection, not silently weakening this static gate.
